content.text:
I ran `npm test` (`node --test`). 7 tests pass and 3 fail. Each failure comes from a one-line predicate change in the last commit (`e4fa6d3 "broken"`). I didn't change anything.

| Test | Expected | Actual | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `findByEmail ignores soft-deleted users` (`tests/auth-service.test.js:5`) | `null` | Alan's user record (`deleted_at: '2026-01-04'`) | `src/services/auth-service.js:5`: the commit removed the `&& u.deleted_at === null` check, so soft-deleted users are returned again. |
| `totalPaidCents counts only paid orders` (`tests/order-service.test.js:14`) | `14600` (4200 + 9900 + 500) | `1350` | `src/services/order-service.js:9`: the filter was changed from `status === 'paid'` to `status === 'quote'`, so it now adds up the one quote order. |
| `uncapturedTotalCents sums uncaptured payments` (`tests/payment-service.test.js:14`) | `9900` | `4200` | `src/services/payment-service.js:10`: the filter was changed from `captured === false` to `captured === true`, so it adds up captured payments instead. |

**The error output is misleading.** In each failure, the top-level message says the `err` argument should have been `null`, and the real assertion failure (the value mismatch above) is nested inside it. That's because `query()` in `src/db.js:31-36` wraps the callback in a `try/catch`. When the test's assertion throws inside the callback, `db.js` catches it and calls the same callback again with the error as `err`. Then `assert.equal(err, null)` fails. So the bugs are only the three predicate changes, not database errors. But this double-call behaviour in `db.js` will hide the real failure in any future test failure too.

status_detail: 3 tests fail: predicate flips in commit e4fa6d3
